record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.original_question: For sequences of regular stationary rotating toroidal Einstein-Vlasov solutions obtained by decreasing the particle cutoff energy E₀ and tuning the angular-momentum parameter L₀, can such a sequence approach an extremal Kerr black hole with compactness Γ tending to 1, or is there instead a strict upper bound Γ<1 or an unavoidable approach to a thin-ring limit? Determine whether higher numerical resolution, a different numerical algorithm, or an analytic obstruction settles the possibility of a quasistationary transition to black holes.

evidence.quote: A central open problem is whether or not a quasistationary transition to an extremal black hole is possible.
The parameter E0 has a natural interpretation as the cutoff energy for the particles, and its presence is important for obtaining solutions with compact support [36].
Note however that the parameter L0 represents a lower bound, resulting in a solution with net angular momentum.
With more computational effort and resolution can one continue this bisection search and reach all the way to a black hole solution? It is not clear that the answer to this question is affirmative.

Hence, from this discussion an essential question arises: is a transition of stationary solutions to black hole solutions possible? Although such a transition has been established in the case of dust there is no a priori requirement that a quasistationary transition to black hole solutions must occur for solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov system.

Perhaps there is a maximum value of the compactness parameter Γ which is strictly below one as in the spherically symmetric case. Perhaps solutions necessarily approach the thin ring limit when E0 is successively decreased independently of the value of L0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the axially symmetric, stationary Einstein–Vlasov system in asymptotic flatness, describing a collisionless ensemble of particles whose phase-space density f on the cotangent bundle is conserved along the geodesic flow and which sources the Einstein equations via its stress-energy tensor. Assume the metric admits two commuting Killing vectors (a timelike ∂_t and an axial ∂_φ), and write f as a function of the conserved energy E and angular momentum L_z along orbits. Restrict attention to ansatzes of the form f = Φ(E_0 − E)·Ψ(L_z − L_0), supported in {E ≤ E_0, L_z ≥ L_0}, that yield regular toroidal matter configurations (the spatial support is a torus topologically encircling the symmetry axis) with finite total mass M and net angular momentum J. Define the compactness Γ = 2M/R, where R is an invariantly defined areal radius of the configuration, so that Γ → 1 corresponds approaching the extremal Kerr horizon ratio J = M^2.

Question: Does there exist a one-parameter family of such regular stationary rotating toroidal Einstein–Vlasov solutions, obtained by decreasing the cutoff energy E_0 and simultaneously tuning the cutoff angular momentum L_0, along which the compactness Γ tends to 1 and the asymptotic Komar quantities (M, J) approach those of an extremal Kerr black hole (J/M^2 → 1)? Equivalently, can a quasistationary transition from regular toroidal Vlasov configurations to an extremal Kerr black hole be realized? Or is every such sequence forced either to satisfy a strict upper bound Γ < Γ_max < 1 or to degenerate into a thin-ring (singular) limit before reaching extremality? Provide either a construction of such an extremalizing sequence or an analytic obstruction ruling it out.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether a quasistationary transition from regular stationary axisymmetric Einstein–Vlasov solutions to an extremal Kerr black hole is possible is explicitly identified as a central open problem. Recent numerical work has produced sequences of toroidal Vlasov solutions approaching very compact configurations and Kerr-like asymptotic quantities, but no construction reaches extremality and no analytic obstruction has been proved. The problem appears to remain open as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Stationary axisymmetric Einstein-Vlasov bifurcations of the Kerr spacetime
status_evidence.snippet: One-parameter families of stationary axisymmetric asymptotically flat solutions to the Einstein–Vlasov system bifurcating from Kerr have been constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Bifurcation families exist but reaching extremal Kerr remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A Monte Carlo approach to stationary kinetic disks in the Kerr spacetime
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical investigation of limits of two-parameter families of stationary Einstein-Vlasov solutions with toroidal configurations approaching extreme Kerr.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to probe but not settle the extremal limit.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic Dyson Rings and Their Black Hole Limit
status_evidence.snippet: For uniformly rotating fluids a quasistationary transition to extremal Kerr is established; the analogous question for Vlasov matter is not.
status_evidence.claim: Fluid analogue solved; Vlasov case still open.
